newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat or down Fri.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat or down Fri.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the fourth day running on Thursday and analysts said more falls in low trade were likely on Friday as investors saved up for copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz's public offering next week.
Analysts said buying might also be dampened by the approaching summer holiday season and September's parliamentary elections but that the market might be reaching a local bottom.
"A majority of stocks should fall (on Friday) but some large-cap firms could rebound and push the index up," said Sebastian Buczek, an analyst at ING BSK Asset Management.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.8 percent to 15,177.2 points and turnover eased 1.5 percent to 100.5 million zlotys ($30.8 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers bt 95 to five with 11 stocks flat.

Some analysts said a central banker's Tuesday warning that Poland faced a Czech-style financial crisis in 1998 due to its widening trade gap was a negative signal but that the finance minister's Wednesday reply that Poland was ready to tackle the problem could help quell concerns.
Marek Belka said foreign direct investment, monetary tightening and a planned leaner 1998 budget would keep the trade gap manageable.

Analysts said Thursday's news that the lower house approved a bill offering the 15 National Investment Fund (NFIs) an income tax exemption for capital gains made on sales of firms in their portfolios could help spur their rebound on Friday.
Others said the news may have already been priced in. The NIF index fell 3.3 percent to 135.5 points on Friday while NFI units fell 1.8 percent to 140 zlotys ($42.9).
